domain_genome.purpose: Answer Win9 / 赢单九步法 sales methodology, customer strategy, project lookup, and evidence-audit questions through Pi-native tools and shared-state evidence.

specialists.purpose: Customer profile and account background specialist
Relationship map, customer facts, and coach analysis specialist
Pain, demand, and business driver specialist
Action plan and project progress specialist
Risk, objection, and recovery strategy specialist

tools.name: win9_methodology_lookup
tools.purpose: Answer simple L1 methodology lookup questions from canonical methodology evidence without spawning step agents.
tools.evidence_policy: Return bounded methodology evidence cards and fail closed on no_match or ambiguous.

tools.name: win9_search_projects
tools.purpose: Search project rows by region, customer, industry, product, budget, quantity, or project name.
forbidden_when: full account planning without user asking for strategy
tools.evidence_policy: Return only adapter rows and disclose missing fields.

tools.name: win9_fetch_customer
tools.purpose: Fetch bounded customer fact bundles for fact-only requests or full orchestration prewrite.
forbidden_when: user explicitly asks for strategy-only reasoning without facts
tools.evidence_policy: Return section counts, previews, missing_data, and tool evidence without raw full dump.

tools.name: win9_run
tools.purpose: Run Pi-native multi-step Win9 orchestration with shared-state evidence.
forbidden_when: fact-only customer request when user says no strategy
tools.evidence_policy: Write run_details and selected step results; final synthesis must use bounded answer packet.

tools.name: win9_read_shared
tools.purpose: Read bounded shared-state files or JSON paths for explicit audit/debug requests.
forbidden_when: broad full JSON dump without user request
tools.evidence_policy: Default to summary; expand only requested files, refs, or jsonPath.

tools.name: win9_merge_results
tools.purpose: Build bounded conclusion-to-evidence audit summaries for an existing Win9 key.
forbidden_when: normal final answer immediately after successful win9_run
tools.evidence_policy: Use summary view and keep final audit answers short.

required_artifacts: customer_facts.json when customer facts are used
eval result JSON for benchmark cases
version ledger entry for release milestones
audit_rules: Do not put full shared-state JSON into model context by default.
Use bounded evidence cards and stable audit refs.
Separate evidence-backed facts from inference and assumptions.
Disclose child errors, missing agents, and partial merge status.

policies: persistent session requires explicit user request
release requires eval, tests, and ledger evidence

known_risks: Full win9_run remains multi-minute for complex orchestration.
Audit answers must remain bounded and not expand unrelated JSON.

runtime_profiles.purpose: Current verified runtime for local Win9 tools, Pi agents, subprocess child runs, evals, and shared-state evidence.
transfer_rules: Pi is the current execution authority for Win9-on-Pi benchmarked behavior.
Keep bounded .win9/shared evidence packets as the default audit surface.
Do not route simple methodology or project lookup tasks through full orchestration.
supported_assets: Pi Win9 local agent prompts and step specialists
Win9 orchestrator extension and bounded shared-state evidence packets
unsupported_surfaces: Gateway/channel delivery is not owned by the Pi runtime profile.
OpenClaw workspace/session APIs are architecture references only unless separately ported.
runtime_profiles.install_or_onramp: Use the Pi workspace references and run the Win9 eval suite before promoting release evidence.
risk_notes: Pi is the certified execution authority; channel delivery and OpenClaw-style agentDir isolation require separate adapter work.
Evidence packets must stay bounded and should not expose raw shared-state dumps by default.

runtime_profiles.purpose: Latest OpenClaw source is the alternate runtime architecture reference for Gateway/channel delivery, isolated multi-agent workspaces, session trajectories, plugin hooks, and runtime ownership boundaries.
evidence_boundaries: OpenClaw runtime id is openclaw; provider, model, runtime, and channel are separate layers.
An OpenClaw agent scope includes workspace, agentDir, auth profiles, and session store; do not reuse agentDir across agents.
Gateway/channel routing owns ingress and egress; it is not the same layer as the domain reasoner.
OpenClaw session and trajectory evidence must stay bounded and sanitized; do not dump raw prompts, tool args, or tool results by default.
Port OpenClaw concepts into Pi/AgentMo through explicit runtime profile transfer rules instead of assuming API compatibility.
transfer_rules: Record runtime ownership explicitly: model loop owner, canonical thread owner, dynamic tool support, native hook support, context lifecycle, compaction surface, and unsupported surfaces.
Preserve OpenClaw isolation semantics: workspace is memory/cwd, agentDir is auth/state/session scope, and sessions are per-agent evidence.
Treat Gateway, channels, nodes, and bindings as delivery/control-plane surfaces around the domain agent, not as the domain genome itself.
Use OpenClaw plugin hooks and session lifecycle ideas as architecture inputs only when the active runtime exposes equivalent hooks.
Keep OpenClaw trajectory/session inspection conservative and bounded when designing AgentMo evidence gates.
supported_assets: Runtime contract and runbook generated by AgentMo
Architecture references for gateway, channel, session, and isolated workspace boundaries
unsupported_surfaces: Not certified as the live Win9 execution authority.
No confirmed parity with Pi Win9 tools, subprocess child runs, or eval harness behavior.
Generated OpenClaw config is an integration starting point, not a validated production deployment.
runtime_profiles.install_or_onramp: Generate with agentmo scaffold --target openclaw, inspect openclaw/RUNBOOK.md, then run OpenClaw-specific integration checks before any runtime promotion.
risk_notes: OpenClaw is recorded as an active alternate architecture reference, not certified runtime parity.
Provider/model/runtime/channel layers must remain separate during porting.
Session trajectory inspection must remain bounded and redacted by default.

discover.purpose: Find the right agent opportunity by collecting domain data, source documents, operational examples, and user needs before designing the agent.
data_sources: Win9 methodology documents and historical workspace archive
Existing Pi Win9 prompts, tools, and eval history
User-stated needs, target scenarios, hard failures, and output preferences
OpenClaw runtime docs and source when OpenClaw is a target architecture
database_outputs: Eval case database grouped by task class
Evidence ledger and version ledger entries
user_need_inputs: What business task the agent should perform
Who will use the agent and in which channel/runtime
What data can be trusted as source of truth
What actions are forbidden or require audit expansion
What output depth, language, and evidence style the user expects
done_when: Data sources are enumerated and bounded
Database or retrieval outputs are named
User needs and hard failures are captured
The agent opportunity is concrete enough to plan

plan.purpose: Turn discovered data plus user needs into a build plan: domain genome, routing strategy, tool contracts, eval design, runtime profile, and release gates.
planning_inputs: Runtime capabilities and boundaries from Pi and OpenClaw profiles
Known failure modes from benchmark history
planning_outputs: Eval cases, rubric, and release gates
decision_gates: No build if source data is missing or unbounded
No build if user need is too vague to evaluate
No build if tool contracts cannot prevent hard failures
No release plan without eval and evidence ledger
done_when: Build outputs and verification path are known

produce.purpose: Use Codex or another coding agent to implement the specified domain agent, generate runtime scaffolds, run tests/evals, repair failures, and record release evidence.
generated_outputs: OpenClaw workspace files and config patch
done_when: Generated agent passes required tests and evals
Runtime evidence is bounded and auditable
Commit/tag can reproduce the agent state
